screening.reason: Analyses ABIDE resting-state fMRI connectivity to classify ASD vs typical control subjects (Inclusion 2, 3)

evidence_spans.text:
The ABIDE dataset: We present our results on the Autism
Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) dataset [4] that con-
tains resting state fMRI data (rs-fMRI) for 1112 patients, as
part of the preprocessed connectomes project
evidence_spans.claim: Study uses the ABIDE preprocessed-connectomes-project resting-state fMRI release of 1112 subjects.

evidence_spans.text:
We follow the same preprocessing pipeline (C-PAC)
and atlases (Harvard-Oxford) as described in [16], in order
to facilitate easy comparison – this resulted in a dataset with
872 of the initial 1112 patients available, from 20 different
sites.
evidence_spans.claim: Analysed cohort was 872 of 1112 ABIDE I subjects from 20 sites, preprocessed with C-PAC and parcellated with the Harvard-Oxford atlas.

evidence_spans.text:
The task is to diagnose a patient as being of two classes
– Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) or Typical Control (TC).
evidence_spans.claim: Main claim is diagnostic classification of ASD vs typical control.

evidence_spans.text:
We use the same 10-fold cross validation as in
[7] of the ABIDE dataset, using their publicly released code
evidence_spans.claim: Evaluation used 10-fold cross-validation, following a prior published split/code.

evidence_spans.text:
We
out perform recent state of the art method [7] for ASD classiﬁ-
cation by nearly 1.5 percentage points, without any additional
information, and using the exact same training protocol
evidence_spans.claim: Proposed bootstrapped G-CNN outperformed the prior state-of-the-art G-CNN method by about 1.5 percentage points in accuracy.

evidence_spans.claim: Classification accuracy on ABIDE: Linear SVM 66.8%, baseline G-CNN 69.50-66.93-66.35% across graph conditions, proposed bootstrapped approach 70.86-67.85-67.39%.

assessments.support: Cohort size and sites reported ("872 of the initial 1112 patients available, from 20 different sites") but no inclusion/exclusion or QC rule stated for which 872 were retained.
Pipeline (C-PAC) and atlas (Harvard-Oxford) are named and matched to a prior paper for comparability.
ASD vs TC label used without stating the diagnostic instrument/source for the label.

10-fold cross-validation reported with a single accuracy per condition and no uncertainty interval; no leakage-control or site-handling statement; site is not a covariate and CV is pooled across the 20 sites.

risk_of_bias.summary: Pipeline and atlas are reported and the 872/1112 analysed subset and site count are stated, but the QC rule for the subset, the diagnostic label source, and leakage/site-handling in the 10-fold CV are not reported, and only single-split accuracies without uncertainty are given.

charting.title: Bootstrapping Graph Convolutional Neural Networks for Autism Spectrum Disorder Classification
charting.disorder_diagnosis: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) vs Typical Control (TC)
charting.specific_features: ROI mean time series, Harvard-Oxford atlas (111 ROIs)
charting.feature_extraction_tools: C-PAC (Configurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes)
charting.model_category: Graph convolutional neural network (ensemble/bootstrapped population graph)
charting.specific_algorithms: Bootstrapped ensemble of graph convolutional neural networks (G-CNN), compared to linear SVM and single G-CNN
charting.validation_methodology: 10-fold cross-validation (same folds/code as prior published study)
charting.key_performance_results: Proposed bootstrapped G-CNN accuracy 70.86% (graph G), 67.85% (naive graph), 67.39% (noisy graph), versus baseline G-CNN 69.50%/66.93%/66.35% and linear SVM 66.8%
charting.summary_key_findings: A bootstrapped ensemble of graph convolutional networks improves ABIDE ASD-vs-TC classification accuracy by about 1.5 percentage points over a prior G-CNN method and is more robust to noisy or naive population graphs.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (ASD vs TC); ABIDE I preprocessed-connectomes-project release; 872 of 1112 subjects, 20 sites
narrative_row.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI parcellated with Harvard-Oxford atlas (111 ROIs); population-graph convolutional neural network ensemble (bootstrapped G-CNN) trained with edge dropout and compared against a single G-CNN and linear SVM baseline; 10-fold cross-validation matching a prior study's splits and code.
narrative_row.outcomes: Bootstrapped G-CNN reached 70.86% accuracy (graph condition), outperforming the baseline G-CNN (69.50%) and linear SVM (66.8%), with improved robustness (67.85%/67.39%) under naive or noisy population graphs versus baseline (66.93%/66.35%).
narrative_row.key_limitations: No stated motion/QC threshold, no diagnosis-source statement, no leakage or site-handling description, single-split accuracy without confidence intervals.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Demonstrates a predictive, ABIDE-I-only, CPAC/Harvard-Oxford population-graph classification approach; cohort subset is a fixed N (872/1112) without a published selection rule.
